first.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure creates temptation to react with promotional_pricing (memory_73), but that risks attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts that don't serve 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' and could trigger margin erosion/race-to-bottom dynamics—so I want to verify the original record before trusting it as a scalable lever. Meanwhile, activation and onboarding completion are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (memory_86 on shortened onboarding, memory_31 on signup simplification) point to onboarding friction as a durable, addressable lever with prior evidence of durable lift. I'm prioritizing simplify_onboarding as the one experiment slot this week since it directly targets a measured regression with previously validated mechanisms, rather than chasing a reactive pricing move whose long-term value tradeoffs are less certain. I'm verifying memory_86 to confirm the onboarding evidence is solid enough to act on now, and memory_73 to check whether the promotional pricing result included any noted risks to customer quality/retention that argue against a reactive price war.

final.rationale: Verification confirms the intended path. exp_73 shows targeted discounting produced strong short-term acquisition (+31% signup, +18% qualified revenue) but a -12% 30-day retention hit, with the source explicitly warning not to generalize discounting as sustainable growth strategy — this directly disqualifies promotional_pricing as a response to competitor pricing pressure, since it optimizes for short-term acquisition at the expense of the stated objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) and would compound the existing risk of attracting low-quality, price-sensitive accounts. exp_86 confirms shortened onboarding drove +13% completion, improved time-to-value, and a +3% retention lift with no downside noted — a durable, positive-retention lever that also directly addresses the current -4% onboarding completion regression and plausibly contributes to the -6% activation decline via improved time-to-value. This is corroborated by memory_31 (signup simplification durably lifting SMB activation), giving two independent supporting records for the onboarding/activation-friction hypothesis versus one now-disqualified record for pricing. I'm running simplify_onboarding as a standard_experiment: not broad rollout, since current conditions (competitor pressure, two simultaneous metric declines) warrant re-validating the lift holds under today's mix before scaling, but not a small_guarded_test either since the mechanism is well-confirmed and time pressure favors decisive but measured action. Flagging downstream_value_risk because SMB churn dynamics are still shifting under competitive pressure and the onboarding fix, while retention-positive, doesn't address the competitor's price positioning directly — that tradeoff should stay visible for future analysts rather than being treated as fully resolved by this one experiment.
